title: Driving on Memory
abstract: arXiv:2608.31029v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: End-to-end autonomous driving models plan future trajectories from raw sensor input. While earlier driving benchmarks often measured deviation from the human trajectory, current benchmarks such as NAVSIM and Bench2Drive evaluate models with richer simulation-based metrics intended to capture safe and compliant driving. A high benchmark score should reflect that a model can understand the scene in front of it and act accordingly. But how much of that score specifically comes from reacting to the dynamic part of that scene?   To probe this, we remove a model's camera input and replace it with memories from prior drives at the same location. The retrieved memories can provide persistent scene information, including road layout and location-conditioned regularities, but not the current traffic state. translated_abstract: 端到端自动驾驶模型从原始传感器输入规划未来轨迹。早期的驾驶基准通常衡量模型轨迹与人类轨迹的偏差，而当前的基准（如NAVSIM和Bench2Drive）则采用更丰富的基于仿真的指标来评估模型，旨在衡量安全且合规的驾驶行为。一个高的基准分数理应反映出模型能够理解其前方的场景并据此做出行动。但这些分数中究竟有多少是来自于对场景动态部分的反应呢？为了探究这一问题，我们移除了模型的摄像头输入，并用之前在同一地点行驶时留下的记忆来替代。检索到的记忆可以提供持久性的场景信息，包括道路布局和与位置相关的规律，但无法提供当前的交通状态。令人惊讶的是，在NAVSIM上，记忆几乎就足够了，在没有实际（观察当前场景的情况下）达到甚至超越了领先的端到端方法的性能。
tldr: 该研究发现，用同一地点的历史驾驶记忆替代实时摄像头输入，在NAVSIM基准上几乎能达到甚至超越领先端到端自动驾驶方法的性能，表明当前基准的高分可能主要来自对静态场景信息的利用，而非对动态交通状况的真实反应。
en_tdlr: Replacing camera input with memories from prior drives at the same location nearly matches or even exceeds leading end-to-end driving performance on NAVSIM, revealing that benchmark scores largely reflect persistent scene knowledge rather than genuine reaction to dynamic traffic.
